item.title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
item.dc:creator: Agathe Ollive, Walter Geibert, Jens Matthießen, Julia Loftfield, Johannes Lachner, Dominik Koll, … (+3)
item.description:
Communications Earth & Environment — matched: ice shelf, Arctic, cosmogenic
Abstract It has been proposed that the Arctic Ocean and Nordic Seas (“the Arctic Mediterranean”) were not only episodically covered by an ice shelf during late Pleistocene glaciations, but disconnected from the North Atlantic and filled with freshwater. Originally based on the widespread occurrence of marine sediments with intervals barren of 230 Th xs (a function of salinity) and low in cosmogenic 10 Be (interpreted as ice cover), this interpretation is highly debated. Alternative explanations state that sediment pulses could instead have diluted both isotopes. Here, we trace the connection between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic using reactive 10 Be/ 9 Be, a water mass tracer resilient to sedimentation variations. We find uniformly low 10 Be/ 9 Be that coincide with the 230 Th xs -minima and more than one order of magnitude below the coeval North Atlantic, consistent with an isolated Arctic Mediterranean. Our findings suggest a highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic, opening questions about its impact on global climate.

item.title: Long-term changes and attribution of lake water levels on the Tibetan Plateau revealed by multisource satellite altimetry data
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Dou, Xin Luo, Chenyu Sun, Zhiqiang Xie
item.description:
Science of Remote Sensing — matched: satellite altimetry
ABSTRACT Monitoring Tibetan Plateau (TP) lakes is constrained by harsh environments and methodological limitations. To overcome the limited spatiotemporal coverage of single-mission satellite altimetry and the shortcomings of conventional linear analyses, we integrated CryoSat-2 and Sentinel-3A/B altimetry observations with a multilevel robust anomaly-detection framework to generate water-level time series for 11 representative TP lakes (2010–2026). Seasonal-Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL) and an XGBoost–SHapley Additive exPlanations(SHAP) framework was subsequently employed to characterize spatiotemporal variations and assess nonlinear associations with five hydrometeorological factors. The generated time series showed strong agreement with in-situ observations (R > 0.94, RMSE: 0.07–0.11 m). Over the 16-year study period, more than 80% of the investigated lakes exhibited sustained water-level increases, with a regional mean rate of 0.27 m yr -1 . However, lake trajectories recent lake trajectories diverged, with some showing accelerated rises and others displaying decelerating or reversed trends. Intra-annual variability also intensified: the mean seasonal amplitude increased by 48.6% (0.17 m) during the last five years. Attribution analysis revealed substantial spatial heterogeneity. While statistical modeling indicated that precipitation (32.5%) and groundwater (21.6%) made the largest regional contributions within the XGBoost framework, individual lakes exhibited predominantly precipitation-dominated, thermal-loss-sensitive, or groundwater-associated response patterns. These contrasting patterns are likely modulated by differences in basin topography, lake morphology, and local geological settings. These findings provide an improved basis for estimating lake-water-storage changes, assessing long-term water-level trends, monitoring overflow and flood hazards, and investigating interactions among lake ecosystems, climate variability, and regional water resources across the TP.
